lines: Funding opportunities for affordable housing developers
The Affordable Housing Trust Fund helps pays housing developers to build or maintain affordable units.
Affordable Housing Trust Fund

San Rafael is committed to safe, stable, and affordable housing for all residents — especially lower- and moderate-income households, seniors, people with disabilities, and those who have experienced homelessness.

To help make affordable housing possible, the City maintains an Affordable Housing Trust Fund. The fund is governed by City Council Resolution 14760. All homes funded through this program must remain affordable for at least 55 years.
Notices of funding availability

The City periodically makes funds available through a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA). The most recent NOFA was issued jointly with Marin County in 2025. The City does not plan to issue a NOFA in 2026.
Rolling applications for property acquisitions

On September 3, 2024, the City Council approved a rolling application process for acquisitions. Up to $250,000 per year is available through this process, depending on available funds. Applicants must meet with City staff before applying. To request an application, email housing@sanrafael.gov.
Community Development Block Grants (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME)

San Rafael works with Marin County to distribute federal housing funds in our area. Funding is awarded on a set cycle, with the County typically announcing available funds in January. For more information, visit the County of Marin website or call (415) 499-6695.
2026–27 Funding Cycle
$1,500,000 in federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds
$700,000 in federal HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) funds
$900,000 in Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) funds, matched by the Marin County Affordable Housing Fund
The application cycle is now closed.
